Visioner BIG | 🇫🇮 🇳🇴 🇷🇺 ‼️ ‼️ Finland and Norway reportedly held secret diplomatic contacts with Russia to prevent a potential military confrontation between NATO and Moscow in the Baltic Sea, according to The Wall Street Journal. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre reportedly used a Russian oligarch as an intermediary before holding direct talks with Vladimir Putin on October 27. According to the report, the two Nordic leaders assured Putin that NATO had no intention of imposing a naval blockade on Russia. The diplomatic efforts reportedly followed warnings from Moscow that it was prepared to carry out preemptive nuclear strikes to protect its interests in the Baltic Sea. The reported contacts highlight the growing danger of military escalation in the Baltic region. Russia’s nuclear threats have raised the stakes of any confrontation with NATO, while Finland and Norway appear to be seeking ways to prevent a direct clash without abandoning their security commitments. The episode also shows how quickly tensions in the Baltic Sea could develop into a much wider European security crisis. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet
